rubric.correct: Every requested fact correct, resolved and summary-supported; equivalent complete meaning accepted.
rubric.partial: A requested fact is missing or unresolved, without a material contradiction.
rubric.incorrect: Any material contradiction, including volunteered contextual claims.

method: Read each complete answer in isolation against the frozen established scope and first twenty entries of expanded-v5/grading-scope.json. No fact borrowed from another question, reader, or summary to complete the answer. Summary/source evidence establishes correctness and support, not omitted answer content. Confidence and support labels are not grades.

cases.answer: Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in their attacking force; apply modifiers. Defense includes defense dice (including mandatory title bonus: Oathkeeper +1, Usurper +2), plus shields rolled, with each double-symbol doubling shields (multipliers stack), plus warbands at targeted sites and defender board force if defender's pawn is at attacker site or any targeted site. Doubles multiply shields only. Bandits add 1 defense per targeted bandit site. Each attack skull immediately kills one warband from the attacker's own force. Count full swords, plus one attack for each pair of hollow swords; an odd leftover hollow sword adds zero. The attacker may sacrifice surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice exactly enough to win, never excess. Attacker wins only when attack strictly exceeds defense; tie or lower is defender victory.
cases.borderline_issue: Whether defense dice are merely mentioned as the pool or are added to the numerical defense alongside the rolled shields.
decisive_answer_quotes: Defense includes defense dice (including mandatory title bonus: Oathkeeper +1, Usurper +2), plus shields rolled, with each double-symbol doubling shields (multipliers stack), plus warbands at targeted sites and defender board force if defender's pawn is at attacker site or any targeted site.

cases.materiality_example: With three defense dice yielding four shields and four eligible defending warbands, the rules give eight defense (the Playbook worked example). Adding dice count as the answer states gives eleven; that changes the winning attack and sacrifices required.
cases.rationale: Incorrect because the actual full sentence materially adds dice themselves to the numerical defense. Other requested facts are supplied, but they do not negate this contradiction. A clearer pool-then-roll explanation would be correct; inserting that explanation into this answer would repair it rather than grade it.
